blocks.html:
Spiritmaster

Role: Ranged magic DPS (pet class). Difficulty: Moderate, deceptively deep. Weapon: Orb.

DPSRangedMagicPet classSolo friendly

Sourcing note: AION 2 launched KR/TW live in November 2025; global PC launch is October 5, 2026. Most guides below are KR/TW-era. Skill and Stigma names are independent fan translations of Korean text, not confirmed global localization strings, so where two sources give different English names for what appears to be the same skill, both are listed. The class is also called "Elementalist" on some wiki sources, an earlier or alternate translation rather than a separate class.

blocks.title: Overview and role
blocks.bodyHtml:
Spiritmaster is a pet-based ranged mage: safer and more forgiving than Sorcerer, but its rotation is deeper than it looks.

Role and playstyle

  • Ranged magic damage dealer wielding an Orb, built around summoning and rotating four elemental spirits (Fire, Water, Wind, Earth) aion2hub.com, date unknown1 fextralife.com, 2026-022
  • Stacks damage-over-time effects, debuffs, and fear-based crowd control from range while the spirits act as semi-autonomous, turret-like damage sources rather than a single persistent pet aion2hub.com, date unknown3

Difficulty

Rated notably lower than Sorcerer: a difficulty-focused tier list places Spiritmaster (referred to there as "Spiritmaster/Elementalist") in its most beginner-friendly bracket, citing "more safety tools than Sorcerer" and a more forgiving learning curve while still delivering respectable damage single source mmoexp.com, 2026-074.

Other guides stress the rotation itself is deceptively demanding: many new players pick it up expecting a simple pet class, then get overwhelmed by the rotation, with the real skill expressed through spirit-cycle management, not simple button-pressing search-summary only, source 403'd exitlag.com, date unknown5.

contested PvE vs PvP ranking

aion2boost.com framing

  • PvE grade: C, "burst is the roster's floor"
  • PvP grade: C, vulnerable to any mechanic that neutralizes summons
  • Praises latency tolerance: "summons keep fighting through lag that cripples every reaction-based kit"

aion2boost.com, 2026-086

Leaderboard-data tier list

  • PvE grade: D-tier, the lowest of any class, only 34 of 800 tracked leaderboard slots
  • Concludes it "asks the most and returns the least in the current PvE meta"

allthings.how, 2026-087

leprestore.com framing

  • Claims Spiritmaster is "the best current PvE DPS recommendation"
  • Claims an A-tier rating as "the biggest winner of pre-launch balance passes"
  • Search-summary only, direct fetch returned HTTP 403, unverified against original text

leprestore.com, date unknown

These three assessments genuinely conflict, from a D-tier "asks the most, returns the least" verdict to an A-tier "biggest winner" claim. Treat Spiritmaster's PvE ranking as unsettled rather than settled.

Its PvP framing is more consistent: sources agree it offers safer, more controlled ranged pressure than melee classes, with strong 1v1 utility from pet pressure plus fear-based crowd control aion2boost.com, 2026-088 pvpbank.com, date unknown9.

Party demand: cited as strong for sustained pressure and solo self-sufficiency but more mechanically demanding in group content where boss movement can disrupt spirit positioning aion2hub.com, date unknown10.

Who should pick it: players who want a self-sufficient solo class with built-in "pet tank" survivability and are willing to learn spirit-cycle management rather than a simple rotation. A reasonable beginner-friendly pick relative to Sorcerer, but not a truly "easy" class once the rotation depth is considered.

blocks.title: Skill priority
blocks.headExtrasHtml: contested naming marketing sources
blocks.bodyHtml:
Both major guides agree Spirit Strike is the top passive; everything else uses different fan-translated names.

Two independent guides give partially conflicting skill names for what appears to be the same core kit; both are reported here (contested naming, single source each for specific priority order).

Guide A (mmoexp, "Warala" mechanic)

Recommends a "Three Spirit Warala" setup using Fire, Water, and Earth spirits, explicitly stating that adding a fourth, Wind Spirit, "slows down the rotation and lowers overall damage efficiency."

  1. Do first: Cold Shock (lifesteal/survival), Flame Transfer (strong damage), a mobility specialization (called essential)
  2. Then: Ancient Spirit (critical timing-dependent), Elemental Fusion (damage and instant-trigger chance)
  3. Later / optional: Fire Spirit as primary summon, Water Spirit secondary, Earth Spirit situational

Passive priority: Spirit Strike and Focus (direct damage) first, then Spirit Regeneration (resource recovery for Ancient Spirit).

single source, spelling unconfirmed mmoexp.com, 2026-071

Guide B (Vortex Gaming)

Recommends investing in only 4 active skills up to level 20 while emphasizing passive development. "Flame Incineration" gets maximum investment (20+) as primary damage dealer, with "Frost Shock," "Elemental Fusion," "Curse," and "Spatial Domination" assigned to macro/mouse buttons.

Passive priority: 1) Spirit Strike, 2) Concentration, 3) Spirit Revival.

single source, machine/fan-translated vortexgaming.io, date unknown2

Both guides agree "Spirit Strike" is the top passive skill priority confirmed across 2 sources.

"Elemental Fusion" is described by both as a proc/trigger effect activated when spirits use their own skills, functioning as the core damage amplifier of the rotation, alongside a similarly-described "Space/Spatial Domination" skill.

A third guide (fori88.co.kr) gives Korean names that partially resolve two of the naming conflicts above. It confirms 냉기충격 (literally "cold-air shock"), the left-click basic attack that increases attack power on hit and is used to fill cooldown windows kr-era single source fori88.co.kr, date unknown3.

It also confirms 화염전소 (literally "flame complete-burn"), the right-click basic attack that provides a skill-speed increase and is alternated with the cold skill via a "left-right cancel" during filler time.

Based on the literal Korean, "Cold Shock" is the more literal rendering of 냉기충격 and "Flame Incineration" (rather than "Flame Transfer") is the more literal rendering of 화염전소, since 전소 means "burned up completely" and gives no basis for a "transfer" translation.

Translation conflict, partially resolved: the confirmed KR names above show "Cold Shock" and "Flame Incineration" are the more literal English renderings of the two basic-attack skills, and "Flame Transfer" looks like a less literal translation of 화염전소 rather than a separate skill. "Space Domination" vs "Spatial Domination," and "Corrosion" vs "Curse" (used as a Stigma name by one guide, a skill by the other), most likely still reflect different fan translations of the same Korean text rather than different skills.
still contested Whether "Cold Shock" and "Frost Shock" name the same skill remains unresolved: a separate English-language search summary describes "Cold Shock" as a distinct signature skill providing the class's only lifesteal, and "Frost Shock" as a different secondary skill assigned to left and right click for maintaining debuffs, implying they are two separate skills rather than one skill under two fan names single source, exact URL not isolated, from a WebSearch synthesis over multiple Vortex Gaming Spiritmaster guides. No official global name has been found for either skill mmoculture.com, 2026-074. Net: treat "Cold Shock" (via 냉기충격) as confirmed as a basic-attack skill; treat whether "Frost Shock" refers to the same skill or a different one as unresolved.
No reliable source found for an explicit "avoid these skills" list. Guide A's advice to skip Wind Spirit in the core 3-spirit rotation is the closest equivalent, but this is a PvE efficiency choice, not a "bad skill." Other sources recommend Wind Spirit specifically for escape/chase/disruption utility, so it is situational rather than universally skippable search-summary only, source 403'd exitlag.com, date unknown5.

blocks.title: Leveling build
blocks.headExtrasHtml: Lv 1 to cap contested kr-era
blocks.bodyHtml:
Max Flame Incineration, Elemental Fusion, and Cooperative Curse first, with Chill Shock close behind; keep spirit summons and dead skills low.

This order comes from Korean class boards (Inven, DCinside) and the fori88.co.kr guide blog, all tracking a skill's own level, breakpoints at 8, 12, 16, and a repeated 20 cap, not character level. Treat the levels below as inferred from the shared Stigma and Daevanion unlock schedule, not stated directly by these guides.

Skill point order

StepWhenSkillTake toWhySrc
1From Lv 1Flame Incineration (화염 전소)Skill Lv maxshared first-priority damage skill everywherefori88 inven
2NextElemental Fusion (원소 융합)Skill Lv maxprimary finisher, needs all four elements activefori88 dcinside
3NextCooperative Curse (협공: 저주)Skill Lv maxthird must-max damage and debuff skillinven dcinside
4NextChill Shock (냉기 충격)Skill Lv 16-20lifesteal plus attack buff, sustains the rotationinven inven
5When points allowSpatial Domination (공간 지배) and Soul's Scream (영혼의 절규)Skill Lv 12secondary combo-link and fear debuff, below the core fourdcinside fori88
6When points allowFour spirit-summon MasteriesSkill Lv 8-16share the Skill Point pool with actives, ranked lowerinven board dcinside

Leave at level 1 or low

  • Shock Release (충격 해제) and Spirit Sacrifice (정령 희생): leave at skill level 1, every source that mentions them calls them low value fori88.co.kr, date unknown1 inven.co.kr, date unknown2
  • The four spirit-summon Masteries draw from the same Skill Point pool as the actives above, so stop at skill level 12-16 instead of pushing to 20 dcinside.com, date unknown3 inven.co.kr, date unknown4
    • 소환: 불의 정령 (Fire), 소환: 물의 정령 (Water), 소환: 땅의 정령 (Earth), 소환: 바람의 정령 (Wind)

Passives

  1. First: Spirit Strike (정령 타격), named the top passive priority across every source that lists passives inven.co.kr, date unknown5 vortexgaming.io, date unknown6
  2. Then: Mental Concentration (정신 집중), raises direct damage and abnormal-status hit rate inven.co.kr, date unknown7 inven.co.kr, date unknown8
  3. Later: Spirit Regeneration / Spirit Communion (정령 회생 / 정령 교감), resource recovery and survival inven.co.kr, date unknown9 inven.co.kr, date unknown10

Level by level

  1. Lv 1-12
    Push Flame Incineration, Elemental Fusion, and Cooperative Curse; spirit priority is contested from the start

    Follow the skill point order above for actives.

    • fori88.co.kr calls Wind Spirit the mandatory first summon for Cooperative Curse synergy fori88.co.kr, date unknown11
    • A separate Inven thread instead ranks Wind Spirit as the single highest-priority summon, kept permanently active on its own hotbar inven.co.kr, date unknown12
    • This conflicts with the 3-spirit Fire/Water/Earth rotation in the Rotation and combos card below, which excludes Wind Spirit mmoexp.com, 2026-0713
  2. Lv 12
    Daevanion board opens: raise skill-level nodes before stat nodes

    A KR source puts Mastery skill-level nodes before stat nodes, then orange end-branch nodes fori88.co.kr, date unknown14

  3. Lv 23
    Stigma opens: slot Grace of Spirit and Ancient Spirit first

    Level 정령의 가호/가오 (Grace of Spirit) then 고대의 정령 (Ancient Spirit) to skill level 20, the two top picks per a dedicated Inven thread inven.co.kr, date unknown15

    • Next, 불길의 축복 (Blessing of Flame) to skill level 20 for party synergy inven.co.kr, date unknown16 inven.co.kr, date unknown17
    • 협공: 부식 (Cooperative Corrosion) to skill level 20 rounds out the core four, a DoT plus roughly 10% all-resistance reduction inven.co.kr, date unknown18 dcinside.com, date unknown19
  4. Lv 23-45
    Keep feeding Skill Points into the core four actives before the spirit Masteries

    This stretch continues the same skill-level order until points allow the spirit Masteries their turn inven.co.kr, date unknown20 dcinside.com, date unknown21

  5. At cap
    What changes: only skill-level breakpoints matter now

    Sources tie the power spike to spirit-cycle mastery, not a level number; see Skill priority above, and the Stigma picks and Daevanion board route cards below, aion2hub.com, date unknown22

Gear while leveling

  • Level Water Spirit and Fire Spirit to at least skill level 16 as a practical floor before investing further inven.co.kr, date unknown23
Spirit priority is contested: fori88.co.kr calls Wind Spirit the mandatory first summon for Cooperative Curse synergy, and a separate Inven thread ranks it as the single highest-priority summon kept permanently active fori88.co.kr, date unknown24 inven.co.kr, date unknown25. The 3-spirit Fire/Water/Earth rotation in the Rotation and combos card below excludes Wind Spirit instead mmoexp.com, 2026-0726.
Avoid: maxing the four spirit-summon Masteries past skill level 16. They share the same Skill Point pool as the four core actives, and Korean guides say directly not to push them to 20, invest to 16 or just 12 instead dcinside.com, date unknown27 inven.co.kr, date unknown28

blocks.title: Stigma picks
blocks.headExtrasHtml: Unlocks lvl 23 confirmed system marketing sources
blocks.bodyHtml:
Stigmas unlock at 23 with 5 slots; PvE favors pet output and DoT uptime, PvP favors debilitation effects.

Stigmas unlock at level 23 with up to 5 slots after the March 25, 2026 KR patch (shared system fact) kr-era, balance may change aion2hub.com, 2026-031.

That same patch added a new Spiritmaster-specific Stigma called "Command: Proxy," which reworks an existing skill named "Kaisinel's Power" into a party buff granting +20% status accuracy/resistance, alongside several spirit skills being converted into AoE effects aion2hub.com, 2026-032.

Early Stigma order

  • Level "Corrosion" and "Fixed Spirit" to rank 5 first
  • Then "Spirit's Grace" and "Fixed Spirit" again
  • Remaining slots from "Shadow of Curse," "Flame Blessing," or additional "Corrosion" depending on preference single source, unconfirmed wording

Vortex Gaming's guide independently lists Stigma priorities as "Blessing of Fire" (accuracy/crit/damage amplification), "Protection" (defensive spirit ability), "Stabilization" (consistency), "Corrosion" (debuff damage), and "Blood Drain" (an HP-based shield, called a strong defensive pick for hard content) vortexgaming.io, date unknown3.

Translation conflict: "Corrosion" and "Blessing of Fire"/"Flame Blessing" appear across both guidance sets above, giving moderate (2-source) confidence to those two specifically, though naming again varies slightly between sources.

PvE vs PvP: aion2boost.com frames PvE Stigma priority as pet output and DoT uptime first, control second; PvP priority as debilitation effects (fear/drain) first, then pet resilience/pressure, then survivability for extended trades aion2boost.com, 2026-084.

Summarized by that source as "pet-facing investment outvalues caster-facing investment at equal cost."

No reliable source found for a confirmed advanced Stigma (level 45) list for Spiritmaster specifically, or for a definitive "spend Stigma Shards on X first" recommendation beyond the general cross-class advice to fund frequently-used Stigmas before spreading investment expcarry.com, 2026-095.

blocks.title: Daevanion board route
blocks.headExtrasHtml: Unlocks lvl 12 confirmed system merged content single-source kr-era
blocks.bodyHtml:
Shared board system; raise main skill levels and take orange end-branch nodes before minor skill levels.

Shared system mechanics (see the Sorcerer guide for the full node-color and board-unlock breakdown): board unlocks at level 12 (Nezekan), with further boards at 20 (Zikel), 30 (Vaizel), 40 (Triniel), and advanced boards at 45 (Ariel for PvE, Azphel for PvP, plus Marchutan and Yustiel referenced in one source) fextralife.com, 2026-011.

Node types: grey = stats (1 point), green = passives (2 points), blue = active skills (3 points), orange = unique board-specialty bonuses (4 points), same source.

For Spiritmaster specifically, aion2boost.com's PvE priority order (pet output and resilience first, DoT uptime second, control third) implies favoring Daevanion nodes that raise spirit-related active skills and their survivability stats before general caster stat nodes marketing source, inferential aion2boost.com, 2026-082.

A KR skill-tree and combo guide gives an explicit Spiritmaster Daevanion priority order:

  1. Raise skill levels on main abilities toward specific targets, levels 16 and 12 are commonly cited breakpoints, before taking orange end-branch nodes
  2. Take orange end-branch nodes for damage amplification, cooldown reduction, combat speed, and crit-damage resistance
  3. Take minor skill levels and multi-hit-related nodes last

kr-era single source fori88.co.kr, date unknown3

This order is single-source and general within the class rather than tied to specific named nodes on the board, but it is the most concrete Spiritmaster-specific Daevanion guidance found so far. It broadly agrees with the general cross-class "prioritize active/blue nodes early" advice.

blocks.title: Arcana
blocks.bodyHtml:
Essential Spiritmaster Arcana picks are Spirit's Majesty, Corrosion, and Inferno; treat exact names as provisional.

Arcana is a shared cross-class system (see the Sorcerer guide for slot types, grades, and Training Arcana values) kr-era, balance may change expcarry.com, 2026-091.

The general DPS-class advice, prioritize cards raising levels on the active skills and passives driving your main rotation, then complete damage-oriented sets, applies to Spiritmaster as a DPS class, but the source gives no Spiritmaster-specific card names or slot priorities.

Spiritmaster-specific picks (single KR guide)

  • Essential: Spirit's Majesty (survival and buff core), Corrosion (DoT and debuff application), Inferno (flame damage output)
  • Optional but recommended: Absorption (30 second cooldown, HP recovery, stable play), Onslaught of Ruin (60 second cooldown, high DPS plus a groggy value of 50, described as less convenient to use)

These are fan-translated names from a single KR guide, not confirmed official terms kr-era single source, fan-translated names fori88.co.kr, date unknown2.

This card list is single-source and KR-era. Treat exact card names as provisional until a second source or global localization confirms them; no Spiritmaster-specific card slotting order beyond "essential vs optional" was found, and no source names cards to avoid.

blocks.title: Gear and stat priority
blocks.headExtrasHtml: mostly single source PvP kit description contested
blocks.bodyHtml:
Orb is the only weapon; Magic Attack, Spirit Efficiency, HP/Defense, Mana Regen, and Accuracy form the stat foundation.

Weapon: Orb (confirmed across all sources). Stat priority, per a PvP-build-focused guide: Magic Attack, Spirit Efficiency, HP/Defense, Mana Regeneration, and Accuracy "form the foundation" pvpbank.com, date unknown1.

  1. Do first: a high-magic-attack Orb with spell power, general advice for DPS classes is to upgrade the weapon first
  2. Then: HP for survivability, since the caster is a sustained-pressure class
  3. Later / optional: Mana Regeneration and Accuracy to round out the "foundation" stats

Detailed gear stat breakpoints from Vortex Gaming's PvE build (single source, KR-era, terminology likely translation-specific): pursue "Perfect" quality options on pants, cloaks, shoes, and gloves single source, numeric values unverifiable vortexgaming.io, date unknown2.

Prioritize Attack Power (cited around 258) and Critical Hit/Accuracy (cited around 147) on stat rolls.

For Awakening (an enhancement tier) prioritize Damage Resistance, Amplification, Critical Damage, and Impact; for "magic stones" (the manastone/godstone-equivalent socket system), "Weapon Damage Increase" is called the most efficient choice.

For PvP, the same source recommends Awakening priorities of HP, Status Effect Resistance, Iron Wall, Impact Resistance, and Damage Resistance, plus a "PVP Damage Amplification" magic stone (Advanced Abyss variant) or "Vitality" as an efficient alternative.

vortexgaming.io claim

Describes Spiritmaster in PvP as "a straightforward damage-trading class with no CC, movement skills, or slows."

vortexgaming.io, date unknown3

Other sources' documented kit

Document fear/root/knockback tools: Soul's Cry, Ashy Call, Earth Spirit bind, Wind Spirit knockback/silence.

fextralife.com, 2026-024 pvpbank.com, date unknown5

Contested: the "no CC, movement skills, or slows" claim is in clear tension with the fear/root/knockback kit documented by two other sources above. This looks like an error or an oversimplification in the vortexgaming.io PvP section rather than a genuine build difference.

Manastone/Godstone-equivalent system (shared, general description in the Sorcerer guide): sockets on gear, Manastones for weapon/armor, Spiritstones for accessories, Godstones for extra combat effects, resettable via soul imprinting kr-era vortexgaming.io, date unknown6.

No reliable source found for confirmed Spiritmaster set-effect names.

blocks.title: Rotation and combos
blocks.headExtrasHtml: confirmed core mechanic marketing sources
blocks.bodyHtml:
Keep a spirit alive and buffed before you summon it; damage collapses the moment a spirit expires.

Core mechanic, confirmed across multiple sources: keeping spirits alive and actively rotated is "the single biggest factor in Spiritmaster output," with damage falling off sharply once summons expire aion2hub.com, date unknown1.

The "Warala" rotation concept (single source, KR-derived term, spelling and translation not independently confirmed): rather than keeping one persistent spirit summoned, the class repeatedly re-summons spirits to retrigger on-summon effects (named "Space/Spatial Domination" and "Elemental Fusion") frequently mmoexp.com, 2026-072.

A 3-spirit rotation (Fire, Water, Earth) is recommended over a 4-spirit rotation, since adding Wind Spirit is said to slow the cycle and reduce overall damage efficiency.

Beginner PvE macro/rotation

Vortex Gaming, single source, KR-era: keep the skill macro limited to one skill ("Flame Incineration"), and manually trigger "Frost Shock," "Elemental Fusion," "Curse," and "Spatial Domination" via separate mouse buttons, pressing them continuously to maintain debuff uptime.

  1. Cast a buff (translated "Flame Blessing")
  2. Open with basic attacks
  3. After using "Spirit's Grace," summon "Fixed Spirit"
  4. At higher gear/skill levels, replace some summons with basic attacks; keep Water Spirit and re-summon it roughly every 15 seconds for its single-target damage

vortexgaming.io, date unknown3 mmom.com, date unknown4 (corroborating the same general macro pattern)

Buff-before-summon timing rule (a specifically called-out beginner mistake): activate buffs such as "Blessing of Fire" and "Protection" before summoning "Ancient Spirit," because spirits inherit the caster's current stat bonuses at the moment they are summoned. Buffing after summoning wastes the effect for that spirit's lifetime mmoexp.com, 2026-075.

Pet/spirit management (confirmed, consistent across 3+ sources)

  • Fire Spirit: offensive summon, applies a Burning DoT and reduces enemy Defense (one detailed source cites 150 damage/sec and a 30% Defense reduction, single-source numeric figure) fextralife.com, 2026-026
  • Water Spirit: healing, cleansing, and shields (same source cites 370 HP per 3 seconds, single-source figure), described elsewhere as the class's primary sustain tool during long fights gamesolusi.com, 2026-077
  • Earth Spirit: gives a damage-reduction shield and can Knock Down/Bind enemies, called "one of the most complete tank pets"
  • Wind Spirit: knocks back and silences, boosts the caster's own movement speed, functioning as the class's escape/chase/disruption tool fextralife.com, 2026-028 pvpbank.com, date unknown9

Combo/utility skill: "Command: Substitution" causes the active spirit to absorb 100% of the caster's incoming damage within a 15-meter radius for 30 seconds, described as a major defensive cooldown that can be paired with a "Spirit Sacrifice" effect for large defensive or offensive payoff fextralife.com, 2026-0210 pvpbank.com, date unknown11.

Situational spirit pairings recommended by one source (single source, contested against the "3-spirit Warala" advice above, which specifically favors Fire/Water/Earth): PvE sustain = Earth + Water; PvP control = Fire + Wind; solo farming efficiency = Fire + Earth contested pvpbank.com, date unknown12.

No reliable, verified source found for a documented dedicated "auto-hunt" skill setup separate from the manual macro descriptions above.
blocks.tags: spiritmaster rotation combos spirits warala macro

blocks.title: Leveling notes
blocks.bodyHtml:
One of the strongest solo classes: the spirit tanks for you, and it wins fights through attrition, not burst.

Solo leveling comfort is rated as strong: Spiritmaster is repeatedly described as "one of the strongest solo classes," with the spirit acting as a built-in frontline/tank so the caster is not the sole damage sponge aion2hub.com, date unknown1 aion2boost.com, 2026-082 (describing "solo safety via personal frontline").

Sustain is comparatively good thanks to Water Spirit's healing/cleanse and Siphon's lifesteal, though damage output is explicitly tied to keeping a spirit alive and correctly positioned, so sustain and damage both collapse together if spirit uptime lapses aion2hub.com, date unknown3 fextralife.com, 2026-024.

No reliable source found with Spiritmaster-specific pull-size guidance. General framing from aion2boost.com is that the class wins fights through attrition rather than burst, so players should "embrace attrition pacing" rather than expect quick single-cast kills aion2boost.com, 2026-085.

When the class "turns on": sources agree the class becomes meaningfully stronger once the player has internalized spirit-cycle management, summon timing, buff-before-summon sequencing, and Elemental Fusion triggers, rather than at a specific level breakpoint. No reliable source ties this to an exact level number.
blocks.tags: spiritmaster leveling notes solo mob density

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.bodyHtml:
Most mistakes come from letting a spirit die, buffing too late, or under-investing in pet-facing nodes.

  1. Treating Spiritmaster as a "simple pet class" and being overwhelmed once the actual rotation depth (spirit cycling, not button-mashing) becomes apparent mmoexp.com, 2026-071
  2. Letting spirits die before re-summoning instead of summoning preemptively to maintain continuous uptime mmoexp.com, 2026-072
  3. Buffing after summoning "Ancient Spirit" instead of before, since the spirit inherits the caster's buffs only at the moment of summoning mmoexp.com, 2026-073
  4. Wasting spirits by summoning them outside the effective combat area, or summoning right before a forced reset/phase change mmoexp.com, 2026-074
  5. Adding a fourth spirit (Wind) to the core PvE rotation when a tighter 3-spirit cycle is reportedly more damage-efficient contested, Wind is also recommended for PvP/escape mmoexp.com, 2026-075
  6. Ignoring positioning relative to your own spirit, losing access to spirit-granted shields/heals that require proximity pvpbank.com, date unknown6
  7. Spamming fear/CC on cooldown instead of using it to lock a specific threat at the right moment, "fear locks opponents strategically, not spam" pvpbank.com, date unknown7
  8. Assuming pet damage alone carries fights in high-end PvE without accounting for boss movement disrupting spirit positioning, which several sources flag as the class's biggest competitive-PvE weakness allthings.how, 2026-088
  9. Underinvesting in pet-facing Stigma/Daevanion nodes in favor of caster-facing ones, when the framing is that "pet-facing investment outvalues caster-facing investment at equal cost" aion2boost.com, 2026-089
blocks.tags: spiritmaster common mistakes pve pvp spirit uptime
